summary: OpenSSH SFTP server provides secure file transfer capabilities over a network. It enables you to copy and manage files remotely using cryptographic protocols. It operates within the standard secure shell architecture.
goodFor: It is a suitable choice if you already manage OpenSSH access on your infrastructure and require standard encrypted file transfers without installing extra daemons.
watchOut: Configuration options can be verbose and tightly coupled to the wider SSH daemon, which may introduce complexity if you only want restricted file transfer access.
deployNotes: As a compiled C binary packaged typically as a deb, it generally requires persistent storage for user data and system-level configuration rather than a separate database.
